- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive but price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model overestimates continuation — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive but price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize reversal — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 2–4 periods.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term (1–3 day) volatility in sentiment-driven markets — smooth forecasts with 3-day moving average if sentiment swings >0.3.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to ignore the trend — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates final price — apply 3–5% downward correction if sentiment is negative or price has shown mean reversion in prior 10 days.
